reviews.text: If you want to go to a veterinary office, that will never answer the phone and is very grungy, dirty and smelly then go here. You can literally be standing there after you took your dog for a routine check up that was supposed to take 40 minutes and ended up taking 3 1/2 hours for no good reason. And you can hear the phone going off in the front desk staff pretending as if they don’t hear the phone never bothering to pick up the phone call. It’s quite terrible. additionally, your pet can go in for a simple ear infection and come out months later completely losing his entire hair and then witnessing other dog parents say similar. They can’t even collect a simple pea sample saying the dog didn’t want to pee, well you had him for 3 hrs maybe offer him some water so he could pee. Just unbelievable they’re power is always out machines never working for exams.Oh and PARKING IS NOT AVAILABLE YOU’RE BETTER OFF PROBABLY WALKING I’LL BLOCK OR TWO BECAUSE TRYING TO CRAM YOUR CAR INTO THEIR SIX PARKING SPOT. LOCATION IS ASKING FOR SOMEONE TO HIT YOUR CAR OR FOR YOU TO ACCIDENTALLY HIT SOMEONE ELSE’S JUST INCONVENIENT.

I had to com here and change my star Fromm 1 to 3. I didn’t like how they give u a price after ur visit but at least they accept vouchers to reduce cost . I want to thank them for accepting low income people with pets.I wish I would’ve found them sooner
Great service caring with a furry family
The lot is really small so there's limited parking spaces. Street parking is always available. Friendly staff, clean facility & the best prices I've encountered.
My first time here, good service, friendliness....

I truly don’t have enough words to express how incredibly grateful I am for Dr. Ramirez and front desk receptionist Arlene. They both went above and beyond for me and my sweet Artie during one of the most frightening moments I’ve ever experienced as a pet parent. 🥹❤️

Arlene is truly one of a kind. From the moment I walked in, she went above and beyond to accommodate us and make me feel at ease. She could tell how stressed, worried, and scared I was knowing that my precious Artie was going into surgery for an intestinal obstruction. Her kindness, understanding, patience, and genuine empathy meant more to me than she probably realizes. It’s rare to encounter someone at a front desk who is not only professional, but truly compassionate and caring. Arlene made an incredibly difficult situation feel a little less scary.

And Dr. Ramirez—what an exceptional veterinarian. You can immediately tell by the way he speaks and explains things that he is incredibly knowledgeable and confident in what he does. But what stood out to me most is that he doesn’t simply do his job—he genuinely cares about the animals entrusted to him. You can feel that he sees every fur baby as more than just a patient.

Dr. Ramirez performed Artie’s surgery and has continued to keep me updated throughout his recovery. I am especially grateful that he was completely transparent with me about ALL of our options and took the time to explain everything. I never felt pressured or like I was being pushed toward the most expensive option. As a pet parent, that honesty and compassion mean everything.

During such a scary and emotional time, knowing that Artie was in the hands of people who genuinely cared gave me so much comfort.

I cannot recommend this location enough. If you love your pets like family, please take them here. You will not regret it.

Thank you, Dr. Ramirez and Arlene, for taking such wonderful care of my Artie! 🥹🐱🐈‍⬛️
Appt was at 3:00 pm. It’s now 5:57 pm still no call; very frustrated

If I could give them 10 stars I would! We've never had a better experience at any urgent care or ER, and I wish they could be our dogs' primary vet. Our two small dogs were unfortunately in the car during a freeway accident, and the team went above and beyond. One had some internal bleeding, the other a tail sprain injury, and they took such amazing care of them. Dr. Thompson and Dr Linney took the time to sit with us and thoroughly walk us through every detail, we can't express how much we appreciate their time and incredible care. Lia and Emily at the front desk were so friendly and sweet, and they truly cared about our pets' wellbeing. Thank you so much again for everything, we absolutely loved this place and highly recommend it to everyone!

Hardly anyone picks up the phone. Have to call 5 to 10 times all day long in order for someone to pick up the call.  Phone would be running for 20 mins and still no one answers.  But when you're there, the receptionists are always chatting.  So, not sure where the phone calls get routed to.  Maybe India?  That's why takes a long time for phone lines to travel abroad.

They even helped me through an animal welfare organization. So I'm very grateful for what they did for Marley. He's passed away now, but I know that while he was there, they took good care of him. Clean, organized and professional. Great first experience. 👍
Very attentive and fairly priced! Thank you for taking good care of my baby!

This clinic has gone downhill over the past few years. Appointments are hard to book, and I’ve left messages with no callback.

More seriously, they run unnecessary tests to drive up the bill. On our last visit, I brought my dog in for what I knew was fleas. He gets anxious at the vet, and staff used that anxiety to justify running tests without my consent, including multiple blood panels and scans, beyond the single blood test I’d approved. They came back saying he might have cardiac issues and intestinal parasites, then ultimately concluded it was just fleas. I had to argue to get over $500 in unauthorized charges removed. My dog spent three hours in the back room and came out traumatized and dehydrated.

The new front desk staff are also unprofessional and short with clients.

After six years with this clinic, I’m done. Looking for a vet with better organization and people who actually care about the animals, not one that treats every visit as an upsell opportunity.

I was a loyal client of this clinic from 2015 onward. Dr. Ramirez always treated my cats with care, and over the years he saved their lives twice. Unfortunately, my experience changed in 2024 when a veterinarian working under his supervision mixed up my two cats, resulting in incorrect diagnoses. Tragically, both of my cats passed away one after the other in 2024. One of my cats suffered from great pain during his last moments, because he was given steroids even though he had heart problems, which was misdiagnosed. I was only finding out about the misdiagnosis from my cat’s autopsy which was done later at an independent lab. Had I did not listen to my gut and gone to get the autopsy, I would be still blinded till this date about the reason of my cats’ passing or shall I say, murder.

This was an incredibly heartbreaking experience for me. I encourage others to ask questions, review their pets’ diagnoses carefully, and use their own when deciding whether to use this clinic’s services.

Dr. Martinez & Dr. Ramirez have been great in taking care of my dog the past two years, however this place needs better organization. I also don’t like the other vet I’ve seen here. Receptionists are some of the rudest I’ve ever experienced at a vets office too.

Why am I 10 minutes early to my appointment, and still waiting 2 hours? Probably because it took 45 minutes for the vet to come into the room just to spend 5 minutes with me and tell me there’s no thermometers in the room, and so now I’m pushed to the back of the like to get a temp check on my dog even though we are now almost 2 hours past my appointment time? Then the receptionist has to nerve to tell me there’s people ahead of me who had appointments AFTER mine? 45 minutes extra to get a temp check after I’ve already been here an hour and a half??

Not worth my time here anymore. Treat your customers time with more respect and give your patients more quality care instead of backing up your schedule. It’s unacceptable.

I took my friend’s rescue for shots waited quite a bit and was witness of an incident that occurred, which raises concerns regarding  client service protocols, particularly when handling walk-in emergencies.

A senior client presented at the clinic with her chihuahua, which was suffering from a visible and distressing medical condition, specifically appearing to be a rectal prolapse. The client was clearly seeking urgent veterinary attention for her pet.

However, the interaction that followed did not meet the compassionate and helpful standards we strive for. The receptionist declined to provide immediate assistance or consultation. Critically, there was no attempt made to contact an on-duty veterinarian for guidance on managing the emergency, nor was any immediate first aid advice or assistance offered to help the client locate an alternative emergency veterinary facility. The client was simply directed to another clinic without further support or empathy, despite the evident distress of both the client and her pet.

This situation highlights a potential gap in our emergency response procedures and the need for comprehensive training on how to professionally and empathetically guide clients through such urgent scenarios, even when direct service cannot be immediately rendered.
Horrible customer service. Their parking lot only has spaces for 5 cars that's including handicapped Good luck trying to find Parking.  The waiting area is small just as bad as the parking lot.
If 0 stars was possible I would proceed with that option!

I cannot recommend Los Angeles Veterinary Care Center, their incredible staff and Dr. Cano highly enough.
I brought my cat, Joni, to them after months of struggling with a chronic illness that had not improved despite numerous veterinary visits, tests, medications, and dietary changes elsewhere. By the time I arrived, I was exhausted, worried, and feeling completely defeated.
From the very first visit, Dr. Cano impressed me with her thoroughness and attention to detail. She carefully reviewed Joni's medical history, listened to my concerns, and immediately ordered a fecal test. The very next day, she personally called me with the results and took the time to explain exactly what was going on, what our options were, and what she recommended moving forward.
What stood out most was how much she cared about making sure I understood the diagnosis. She didn't just prescribe a treatment and send us on our way. She explained the parasite, discussed the risks and benefits of different treatment approaches, and created a management plan tailored specifically to Joni's situation. She recommended Biome food, probiotics, fiber therapy, and hygiene protocols to reduce reinfection. She even followed up with articles and supplement recommendations so I could educate myself and become an active participant in Joni's recovery.
The difference was remarkable.
Within two weeks, Joni's diarrhea had completely stopped. Her fur began growing back, her energy returned, and for the first time since I adopted her, I got to see her true personality emerge. She became playful, happy, and comfortable again.
She is now completely parasite-free.
As pet owners, we trust veterinarians with the lives of our animals. What I found at Los Angeles Veterinary Care Center was not only medical expertise but also compassion, communication, and genuine dedication to patient care and she always answers all of my questions. Dr. Cano treated both me and my cat with kindness and respect throughout the entire process, and I will always be grateful for what she did for Joni. My new cat Birdie, is also under her care.
Without question, this is the veterinary clinic I trust and recommend whole-heartedly.

Affordable and very informative. They told me stuff that my dog needed that my previous vet didn’t mention. Reasonable wait time and very fresh inside. Very patient as well. Definitely coming back, if needed.
LAVC and Dr Ramirez did a wonderful and thoughtful job with my cat’s teeth extractions for a fair price.

Seem to went well but my cat has been unable to close his mouth properly since. Told one of the vets about in a future visit and they basically shrugged like it did not matter. The staff at this establishment are incredibly rude and unprofessional. Despite my attempts to remain calm after they failed to assist me, I was met with rudeness and a lack of helpfulness. When I tried to contact them after the fact, the lady at the front desk quickly introduced herself and put me on hold without informing me that she would do so. She then left me waiting for 20 minutes. When I called back, she simply sent me to voicemail.

It has taken a couple of months for me to be able to write this review because it involves my dog passing a few days after being seen by Dr. Cano at this LAVC office.
I adopted a puppy (estimated 10 months) from the Downey SEAACA animal shelter on a Thursday evening. They were transparent that she had kennel cough, a common ailment in animal shelters. I adopted anyway because I figured the pup would have a much faster recovery in a home with personal attention. I noticed she was not improving and, in fact, getting way worse: extremely lethargic, not eating or drinking. She struggled to have energy to walk even a few feet. We took her to LAVC that Saturday and submitted the one page veterinary record we had from the shelter showing shots/treatment given by them. We needed a full check-up since it's a new adoption plus specific advice on her worsening condition and the the kennel cough. After examination, Dr. Cano stated tests showed nothing else wrong with her besides some liver numbers being slightly less than optimal and sent us home with expensive liver supplements. I also noticed the pup has been dewormed unnecessarily since she had just undergone that treatment a few days prior according to the vet record I had submitted. Dr. Cano also prescribed cough tablets even though pup was not really coughing (another sign that kennel cough has progressed to pneumonia I learned later).
The following Tuesday evening we noticed labored breathing and we took her to an emergency animal hospital in Pasadena who immediately admitted her. Turns out she had full blown pneumonia. They did everything they could. We spent several thousands of dollars to try to save her (oxygen chamber, round the clock care) but the pneumonia was too advanced and she died that Thursday night.
I want to stress that this is all in a week's time, and she had been seen by Dr. Cano at LAVC just 3 days prior to being admitted to the emergency hospital with an advanced case of pneumonia. The animal hospital in pasadena stated she was the sickest dog in their care at that time. I cannot know for sure whether there was negligence in LAVC not detecting the pneumonia just 3 days prior. If they did not have the facilities to treat that condition, I would have much preferred that they turn me away and send me to an animal hospital instead of treating her for things she did not need and sending me home with a $500 vet bill that made no difference to the actual condition that was about to kill her a few days later.
My other healthy dog had previously seen Dr. Ramirez at LAVC for a limp and there was no issue with that appointment. My pup's condition improved with pain and inflammation meds, just as Dr. Ramirez predicted.
Do with this information what you will. From this experience I deduce that the quality of treatment may vary depending on the vet that you get. Personally, I am gutted that this poor shelter pup, who we didn't even get to name, was sent home with me to die possibly because I may have chosen the wrong vet. I often wonder if she would have lived had I taken her somewhere else that Saturday. Would those extra days have given her little lungs a chance to fight? I'm so incredibly sad about the whole ordeal.
Great facility with caring staff and Drs.
I've been coming here since 2018. Three dogs. All great Vets. Highly recommend.
Excellent service and good care for pets

I had such a positive experience here and am truly grateful for the kindness and care shown to both me and my cat.
My cat has had a large lump on his arm for some time, and I came in feeling very anxious and worried. The staff took the time to examine him thoroughly and explained everything clearly and honestly. They reassured me that he is otherwise healthy and that the lump can be removed through a cosmetic surgery if we choose to move forward, which gave me a lot of peace of mind.

When my cat became stressed and reactive during the visit, the team handled it with patience and compassion. Instead of forcing anything, they adjusted the plan and provided medication to help him relax for his next appointment so blood work can be done safely and calmly. I really appreciated that they prioritized his comfort and well-being.

The estimates for blood work and surgery were clear, reasonable, and far more manageable than I expected, which was a huge relief. I never felt judged or rushed; just supported and listened to.

This clinic truly cares about animals and their owners. I’m very thankful to have found them and would absolutely recommend them to anyone looking for compassionate, honest veterinary care.
My friend recommended me this place. The staff was courteous and respectful-super friendly and sweet. They were really busy. The rates were really affordable too. I can't say enough nice things
Staff was super nice. Dr. Martinez was great with my cat.  I really like the vibe.

I’m very disappointed with this clinic. This is the second time they charge me a lot of money and don’t help at all. They only care about payment, not about giving real attention or finding what’s wrong with the pet. I trusted them again hoping for a better experience, but it was the same situation. I don’t recommend this place — they take advantage of people who come worried about their pets.

Very friendly staff, and I like that they don't take long to help you. Keep up the good job.

Overall a good option but getting an appointment is difficult. I just wish getting in and speaking to a person would be easier.   As a result I've moved on and found a other office that is further away but more responsive and available.

Best vet spot I have taken my dogs to in LA. The Vets are personable and treat our pets with care and the prices are reasonable. Still the cheapest prices for the best service of any vet place I have been to. You can find cheaper places but I guarantee the wait times will be longer.

Calling to make a appointment is ridiculous, them
Telling you there’s one person ahead and still making you wait more than 30 min is insane!!

I have been a patient at Los Angeles Veterinary Center for 8 years.

I began taking my pets to the Boyle Heights facility, I had just recently started taking my pets to the Jefferson Blvd facility.

On Saturday, August 2, I was treated horribly by Dr. Cynthia Mata and the two receptionists. Our appointment was at 10:45am. We arrived on time and still had to wait almost an hour to be seen. When Dr. Cynthis Mata finally entered the room, she said “I’m sorry for the wait, I had an emergency”

Upon entering, Dr. Mata asked me why I was there. I understand this is protocol, however, they called me twice in the morning before my appointment to confirm, why would the Dr. Ask me why I was there. We were there for a chest X-ray and an RSV panel and anything else the Dr. recommended. I was prepared to pay for anything to get my cat the help she desperately needed.

My cat is very ill. This was my third visit taking my cat to the Los Angeles Veterinary Center.

My cat has been having trouble breathing and nose bleeds since May 2025.

On the 2nd visit, Dr. Cynthis Mata told my boyfriend to euthanize our cat without doing any tests at all.

I found this statement to be cold, callous, lacking compassion, and highly unprofessional.

I understand there comes a point in treatment of a sick animal where euthanasia is the best option for the animal, however, this conclusion usually happens after all tests have been exhausted.

This was only the 2nd time visiting the Los Angeles Veterinary Center to assess what was wrong with my cat.

On the third visit, August 2, 2025, Dr. Cynthia Mata was took her coldness and unprofessionalism to a whole new level.

I asked Dr. Mata why she felt it was appropriate for her to tell my boyfriend and I to euthanize our cat at the last appointment. Apparently this question set her off. She said that X-rays and treatment don’t have any guarantees to figure out what is wrong. She made this statement before doing any tests.

After doing the physical examination on my cat. She said she felt a lump and walked out. I was deeply concerned by this. Why would a Dr say something as concerning as that and then leave the room abruptly? Going back to her “emergency” earlier, wouldn’t the lump in my cat’s throat be considered an emergency as well? She did not leave the room because she considered my cat’s “lump” an emergency, I am still not sure why she left.

Before she left, she told me in addition to the x-ray and rev panel, we could also add a fungal exam.

Before she left I asked her for 2 estimates, one with the fungal exam and one without.

She sent in one of the receptionists to give me my estimates. However, the receptionist only brought in one estimate without the fungal exam.

I told the receptionist I asked for 2 estimates. Dr. Cynthis Mata walked in and said “I didn’t think you wanted to pay for the fungal exam which is why I didn’t print it out” This statement was deeply offensive. I asked her what she meant by that statement. She did not have an answer. I was prepared to pay for anything to help my sick cat. I just wanted to see the cost differences. The Dr. assumed i “didn’t want to pay for the treatment” and I was highly offended by this. All she and the receptionists had to do was print out 2 estimates for me to compare. Yes they took it upon themselves to assume what I wanted to pay for.

After I asked her why she only printed out one estimate without the fungal exam and what she meant by that statement about assuming I “didn’t want to pay for it” She very coldly stated “You know I can refuse services to you right?” I asked her “are you refusing services to me?” She said “You know what, I am refusing services to you”

At this point I was bewildered and flabbergasted. Nothing I said or did warranted a reaction like this from Dr. Cynthia Mata and the receptionists.

(FULL REVIEW IS ON YELP)
Dr. Ramirez and the staff here are very kind and helpful.  This place is also very reasonably priced.  Thanks for taking such good care of my pups.

Very nice staff, you do have to make appointments in advance.

Highly, highly, highly recommend this vet office. I came here based on the reviews after a night of staying up with my dog who had foxtails in her nose. I arrived about 30 min before they opened, and there were people in line. I recommend 40-45 min early for those without appointments.

The staff was super nice, the vet was quick and did an AMAZING job. She was able to get all the foxtails out, and the price was reasonable.

Competent, nice, and did a great job. A+++

Edit:

I’m knocking down the stars I left in the first review to two stars. I came in with a voucher to get rid of foxtails in my dog’s nose, but they didn’t do the work. I came in on the first of the the month for foxtail and debris removal. They gave her vaccines and blood work but left the foxtails in her nose. Since I came in with a voucher, the bald male doctor said ‘you can ask for another voucher to get the work done’. So I asked for another voucher and the organization who provides them only provides one per year. So my dog still has debris in her nose.

Based on this last interaction I wouldn’t recommend this place anymore. I may finish the work she needs here as she’s already in the system, but won’t return after. I can’t afford the work they quoted me until I get paid. And if I pay it all myself it cuts into other bills and necessities. They seem to be in it for the money, and I get it, they have to pay bills. But lying to me saying that I can get another voucher when I can’t, and leaving my dog with foxtails in her nose is horrible.

Help my dog get the proper help she needed

I made this a 2 because they always tell me different information on the phone then they do in clinic. i always ask if I can bring my dog for an appointment to get his flee and tick and they have told me x3 times no and then when I come it its always he needs to be present and we need a test I think its a constant issue I have been dealing with for several years they always just brush it over and its really inconvenient when I have to drive so far and I could have brought my dog. Please do better with looking up information and communication.

Disorganized, inconsistent, and unprofessional. Depending on who picks up the phone, you’ll get a different version of the truth. Tried to get a simple travel certificate for my dog, it’s a 10-minute appointment, no shots, just paperwork. Called Monday (6/16), they said no appointments available until the 25th, which is too close since we fly on the 30th.

Told me to call back Friday for a same-day slot. I called at 8am, nothing. They then suggested a different location. That one only had the “certificate doctor” on Mondays but squeezed me in for 6/23 (still risky since I’m traveling on the 30th). Called the original location again, and suddenly they did have a spot on the same day. Great.

Show up at 2:10 for my 2pm appointment after visiting a friend in Saint Johns in Santa Monica and 1.5 hour traffic. Wait 10 minutes to even be checked in, then told I’m “20 minutes late” and can’t be seen. The receptionist even asked the other, in front of me, how long I’d been standing there. “Couple minutes tops.” What a loser?

I wait patiently another 30 minutes, only to be told the doctor won’t see me. But they now magically have a 6/23 opening after all.

The other location called me on Monday morning just to tell me they won’t be able to take me in because now it’s too close and they suddenly need 10 full days for the certificate (which is a lie). Also, then why do you give an appointment in the first place?

I hope the staff find more joy in their work soon, because it sure didn’t show. You work with animals, after all, but still clearly hard to find some kindness in your heart. And no one is business oriented either - those certificates aren’t cheap and I have a lot of friends who travel with their pets all the time, and I’ll make sure they won’t be coming here.
